newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND'S WANING FLOODS STILL CAUSE NEW SUFFERING.
newsitem.headline: POLAND'S WANING FLOODS STILL CAUSE NEW SUFFERING.

text.p: As Poland's flood disaster appeared to be nearing an end on Wednesday the deadly waters were still aiming last spiteful blows at suffering communities.

Flood crisis committee official Marek Sobczak said that after weekend rains a smaller version of the high-water swell that previously smashed into the southwestern cities of Opole and Wroclaw was again advancing north up the Odra river.
He told Reuters the wave was likely to reach Opole late on Wednesday but that no repeat of the calamity that drowned its downtown blocs in two metres of water was likely now.
"Considering the state of the Odra and of the dykes we should not expect that there will be another catastrophe on the same scale as early this month," Sobczak said.
He said that in Wroclaw further north, the residential estate of Zacisze was likely to again be soaked.
He added that a reversal in the flow of the Warta river as it met the brimming Odra by Kostrzyn on the German border was likely to cause floods as the tributary backed up.
"The reversal of the Warta is dangerous," he said.
Other communities had already fallen victim to the latest rains which heaped misery on a country reeling from the effects of downpours more than two weeks ago.
Sobczak said that 5,360 hectares had been flooded overnight from Tuesday to Wednesday, with the Czestochowa, Kalisz, and above all Wroclaw provinces most affected.

Many of the hundreds of thousands of people whose homes had already been damaged were still waiting for the waters to drain so they could begin to clean up and start the daunting task of reconstruction.
According to Sobczak 518 communities were still flooded, 12 of them totally, out of a total of 1,278 towns and villages that had been struck by the disaster.
Of the 5,972 sq km of Poland that had been swamped, 2,710 sq kms were under water, while 52,300 evacuees were still unable to return to what remained of their homes.
Police told Reuters the confirmed death toll throughout the flooding was now 55.
Hope came from forecasters who said there would be no heavy rain over south and west Poland in the next two days, although there might be scattered rains there.

"In the coming two days we are expecting occasional showers over the area...but there will be no heavy, continual rains," an official of Poland's Meteorology and Water Management Institute told Reuters. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
